findings.title: Change-email form verifies the password of the submitted user id, not the session user
findings.mechanism: The form handler looks up the account by the user_id field in the POST body and checks the submitted password against that account, then changes the email of the session's account.
findings.evidence: Reproducer: POST with user_id of the attacker's own second account and that account's password; the session account's email changes.

security_claim.preconditions: a session on the victim's account (e.g. an unlocked shared computer)
security_claim.gain: change the account email, and so take over the account, without knowing its password

findings.title: Address blocklist stops password login but not API-token requests
findings.mechanism: The blocklist check runs in the login view only; the API-token authentication policy never consults the address blocklist.
findings.evidence: Reproducer: blocklist 203.0.113.9, upload with a token from that address: 200.

security_claim.attacker: a user whose address is blocklisted
security_claim.preconditions: a valid API token created before the ban

findings.title: Admin 'delete user' crashes on service accounts, so staff cannot remove them
findings.mechanism: The admin view dereferences user.email, which is None for service accounts; the delete is rolled back.
findings.evidence: Reproducer: admin deletes a service account: AttributeError, 500.

security_claim.gain: the account cannot be removed by staff

findings.title: Security notification emails are lost when the task queue is unavailable
findings.mechanism: Notifications are enqueued after commit; if the broker is down the enqueue raises and is swallowed.
findings.evidence: Reproducer: stop the broker, log in from a new device: no email is ever sent.

security_claim.gain: victims are not told about a new login

findings.title: A request in flight during logout writes the session back, re-authenticating it
findings.mechanism: Logout clears the session, but a concurrent request that loaded the session earlier saves it on response.
findings.evidence: Reproducer forces the interleaving with events: the old session is valid after logout.

security_claim.preconditions: the attacker holds the victim's session cookie
security_claim.gain: the session survives the victim's logout

findings.title: Authenticated users can upload many large files slowly to tie up workers
findings.mechanism: Upload size is checked after the body is read; each upload holds a worker until the body arrives.

security_claim.preconditions: an account and a project; uploads are rate limited per user
security_claim.gain: worker exhaustion while the uploads last

findings.title: Unauthenticated request with a long Accept-Language header holds a global lock for seconds
findings.mechanism: Locale negotiation runs a quadratic parse while holding the process-wide translation lock; every request waits for that lock.
findings.evidence: Reproducer: one 64 KiB header holds the lock for 4.1 s; concurrent requests wait the full time.

security_claim.gain: every request on the worker stalls while the parse runs; a few requests per second stall the site

findings.title: Archive upload validation has no decompressed-size cap (decompression bomb)
findings.mechanism: Archive members are decompressed fully before validation; a TODO in the source notes the missing cap.
findings.evidence: Reproducer: a 400 KiB archive inflates to 3 GiB during validation.

security_claim.gain: memory and CPU exhaustion on the upload worker

findings.title: Two ZIP readers disagree on member names when a Unicode path extra field is present
findings.mechanism: The validator reads raw names; the metadata extractor honours the Unicode path extra; a crafted archive shows each a different member.
findings.evidence: Reproducer: the two readers list different members. No installer was tested.

security_claim.gain: installers may install files the validator never saw

findings.title: Password-confirmation endpoint reveals whether a password is correct
findings.mechanism: The endpoint returns 403 for a wrong password and 200 for a right one; it uses the login rate limits.
findings.evidence: Reproducer: the response code differs for right and wrong passwords.

findings.title: Static documentation pages lack Content-Security-Policy and Permissions-Policy headers
findings.mechanism: The static file route bypasses the middleware that adds security headers.
findings.evidence: Reproducer: curl -I on /docs/ shows no CSP header.

security_claim.gain: easier exploitation of any future XSS

findings.title: Password-reset limiter answers 429 only for ordinary accounts, revealing which accounts are staff
findings.mechanism: The per-user reset limiter is skipped for privileged accounts, so repeated requests return 429 for ordinary accounts and never for privileged ones.
findings.evidence: Reproducer: 10 resets for an ordinary account give 429; for a staff account, never.
